Title: EventPipeline
Content:
Custom publish/subscribe system with automatic cleanup of disposed subscribers. Replaces standard .NET events.

Contains: IEventPipe interface, EventPipe (non-generic) class, EventPipe of T generic class, and the EventPipeline abstract base class.

Usage: subclass EventPipeline, define InvokePipeline and ConfigurePipe methods. Consumers call ConfigurePipe to subscribe and get an IDisposable that removes the subscription when disposed.

Thread safety: _pipes is a ConcurrentDictionary. InvokePipeline snapshots the list before iterating. ConfigurePipe has a small read-then-write race that is acceptable in practice.

Known issues: 1) InvokePipeline cleanup is a no-op (pipes.RemoveAll on local snapshot). 2) EventPipe.Invoke(object obj) silently drops the argument. 3) EventPipe of T .Invoke() throws NotImplementedException. 4) The _lock field is never used; dead code.
